spot: Main parking / developed core (Park Office, amphitheater, picnic shelter, geocaches)

Developed lot sits beneath the quarry cliff; view is blocked/enclosed, not a sweeping panorama.
Developed core has buildings, pavilions, lot; no natural rock crevice/niche is the operative feature here.
A surface hide is possible (geocaches exist), but there is no natural ledge/hollow/boulder base; man-made structures only.
Operative landmarks are Park Office/amphitheater/shelter, not a boulder/outcrop/sittable rock.
Rocky Face Branch headwater and the wetland are nearby in the developed core, but the lot itself has only man-made water; adjacency is weak/incidental.
Developed clearing with forest at its edge where trails enter, but this is a paved/built clearing, not a natural forest-meets-meadow edge.
All trailheads originate here and the paved ADA track loops from the lot; quintessentially trail-accessible and easy footing.
Drive-up lot directly off Rocky Face Church Road; 0 mi from road, trivially satisfies the bound (but fits almost anywhere, weak).
Highest-traffic, most exposed hub in the park (~200k visitors/yr pass through); opposite of secluded/off the obvious.
No twin-crag gap/saddle framing the lot; it is open flat developed ground.
